status: planned - no participants tested and no EEG recorded yet
name: Validation pilot - staged theft (example stimuli)
provenance: Example stimuli for the staged-theft scenario in the BrainLock Validation Pilot Plan. The lab's stimulus author replaces these with the real scenario details before pre-registration and keeps the real probes away from examiners and participants. Probes are known only to knowledgeable-group participants through the staged theft itself.

analysis.primary: dual bootstrap (correlation 300-900 ms, amplitude 300-700 ms), 1000 iterations
analysis.secondary: Dr. Farwell's analysis method, only if provided in writing

study.title: BrainLock Validation Pilot

arms.description: Carries out the staged theft; knows the six probe details
Does an unrelated task of the same length; never learns the probe details
Staged theft, then trained in covert responses to chosen irrelevants (Rosenfeld et al., 2004)

study.blinding: Examiner and analyst do not know arm assignment; the lab keeps the assignment key

successCriteria.target: 5% or less of naive participants called present, upper 95% confidence limit 10% or less
80% or more of knowledgeable sessions with a verdict called present
Sessions with under 80% target responses flagged and analyzed both ways
